subject: Preflight: dedicated GPU slice request for NimbleHealth pilot
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, j.patel@nimblehealth.com
Cc: ops@nimblehealth.com
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:23:00 -0800
Subject: Preflight: dedicated GPU slice request for NimbleHealth pilot

Hi all,

Quick context: NimbleHealth (external) is ready to run a production-like pilot for their clinical summarization feature. They want predictable latency and data isolation, so the ask is a short-term dedicated slice rather than hosted burst.

High-level request:
- Window: 2026-11-09 -> 2026-11-30 (3 weeks)
- Quantity: 4x H100 (or equivalent) GPU slots pinned to one pool
- Autoscale: need an exception to the default Dedicated autoscale cap to allow burst up to 2x (so 4 -> 8) during business hours for load tests and demo days
- Canary: will run a canary on a 7B distill model first, then a 70B quantized model the last week

What I need from infra/product/ops:
1) Feasibility check on reserving 4 H100 slots in us-west region for those dates
2) Short list of operational constraints (preemption window, eviction policy, billing impact)
3) Quick approval path for a temporary autoscale exception and how to document it (procurement + ops sign-off)

I've attached a short preflight checklist and the NimbleHealth canary plan. Nimble's PM (j.patel) is copied to confirm dates.

If we can confirm availability by EOD Friday (2026-11-05) Nimble will sync procurement and we can finalize the doc.

Thanks —
Ava Chen
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.com

Attachments: dedicated_preflight_checklist.xlsx, pilot_canary_plan_v1.pdf

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: j.patel@nimblehealth.com
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Preflight: dedicated GPU slice request for NimbleHealth pilot

Ava — thanks for the clear ask. A couple of clarifying Qs before I lock anything down:

1) Sustained tokens/sec and 95th p95 latency SLO during demo days? (helps size the pool and gating for autoscale)
2) Are the 4 slots intended to be continuous (pinned) or can they be shared across a reservation window (time-blocked)?
3) For the autoscale exception: do you need the platform to automatically scale to 8, or just allow manual burst by on-call? Automatic exceptions require a short runbook + risk sign-off.
4) Will Nimble use KV/prefix caching or rely on cold starts? Cold-start-heavy workloads might push us to recommend 6 slots instead of 4.

If you can drop numbers for item (1) I'll run a quick capacity check with the pool team.

—Markus
Director, Capacity Planning
markus.klein@redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 14:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Preflight: dedicated GPU slice request for NimbleHealth pilot

On Wed, Nov 04, 2026 at 10:12 AM Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com> wrote:
> Ava — thanks for the clear ask. A couple of clarifying Qs...

Quick answers from product/ops side (summary of infra check):
- Availability: We have capacity in the us-west H100 pool for 2026-11-09 -> 2026-11-30, but it's near-contested for week of 11/16 (model-sweep test windows). We can carve 4 slots if we accept a soft-preemption window on 11/16-11/18.
- Recommended config: 4x H100 pinned, with a reservation lease window (09:00-19:00 PST) to reduce cross-team preemption outside demo hours.
- Autoscale: We can provision a temporary pilot-burst-policy that allows automatic scale up to 2x for 3 discrete burst events per day. This requires:
  * a 1-page runbook (ops) describing automatic fallback to fallback-model variant, and
  * procurement acknowledgement of potential additional usage costs.
- Sizing guidance: If Nimble intends to serve 300 concurrent small requests (median 40 tokens) with p95 < 400ms, four H100s should be adequate with prefix caching. If they expect sustained streaming loads (large outputs), consider increasing to 6.

Action items for Ava/Nimble:
- Confirm expected concurrency and p95 target (numbers) by EOD Friday 11/06.
- Approve reservation lease window and accept soft-preemption on 11/16-11/18.

I'll draft the runbook skeleton and the autoscale exception ticket once we have the numbers.

—Marcus Lin
Principal Product Manager, Dedicated
marcus.lin@redwood.com

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, j.patel@nimblehealth.com
Date: Mon, 08 Nov 2026 15:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Preflight: dedicated GPU slice request for NimbleHealth pilot

Thanks Marcus/Markus — quick update and next steps from our side.

Nimble confirms the following numbers for the pilot:
- Expected concurrent requests during demo windows: 220 users (concurrent), median payload ~45 tokens
- p95 latency target: <= 350ms for 7B model canary; for the 70B quantized canary we accept p95 <= 800ms during the final week
- They will enable prefix caching for stable traffic and will seed the cache before demo days

We accept the reservation lease window (09:00-19:00 PST) and the soft-preemption window 11/16-11/18. Nimble also acknowledges potential overage charges if we hit the autoscale cap.

Please proceed with:
1) Carve 4x H100 slots in us-west with the lease window and soft-preempt clause for 11/09-11/30
2) Open a temporary autoscale exception ticket (pilot-burst-policy) allowing automatic 2x bursts (3 events/day) — route to procurement for cost acknowledgement
3) Marcus: share the one-page runbook + eviction rules by COB 11/09 so Nimble can review and sign off

I've attached the completed preflight checklist and the signed canary intent from Nimble (they uploaded a countersigned copy to the shared Drive link).

Nimble PM: j.patel@nimblehealth.com — let us know if any of the above needs to change; otherwise we'll treat this as approved and move to ticketing.

Best,
Ava Chen
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.com

Attachments: dedicated_preflight_checklist.xlsx, pilot_canary_plan_v1.pdf
